epics.title: Status-Driven Agent Home

items.title: Build the Home dashboard aggregation service
items.description: Build a project-scoped, permission-gated server module that composes the Incomplete Pipeline groups, the five Artifact Cycle Time medians, the My Work counts and median, the Open Bugs on PBIs counts, and the Developer-to-production median into the five dashboard tile payloads. The module applies each source module's existing permission check before returning that tile's data and falls back to last-known values for the Azure DevOps- and Releases-backed tiles when those sources are slow.
definitionOfDone: A single per-tile query interface returns each of the five dashboard payloads scoped to the caller's project and permissions
Each tile payload omits data the caller's permission does not allow, rather than returning it and hiding it client-side only
Azure DevOps- or Releases-backed tiles degrade to a last-known value instead of failing the whole dashboard response when that source is slow
Unit tests cover: a fully-populated project, a project with no qualifying data for a tile, and a slow/failing upstream source
technicalDependencies: Existing Interview, PRD, Design Prototype, Design Doc, and Test Case read models
Existing My Work session and readiness data
Azure DevOps work-item and Release production-deployment access
nonFunctionalRequirements: Apex-local tile payloads complete within 2 seconds at P95 under 100 concurrent Home loads
Azure DevOps- and Releases-backed tile payloads complete within 5 seconds at P95, or return the last-known value instead of blocking

items.title: Compute artifact cycle time medians
items.description: Build the calculation that, per artifact type, finds the median duration from creation to that type's own done event — Interview Mark Complete; PRD, Design Prototype, and Design Doc owner final approval; Test Case suite ready — over completed items in a rolling 90-day window, using a done-event timestamp frozen at the moment of that transition.
definitionOfDone: Median is computed independently per artifact type over completed items in the trailing 90 days
An artifact type with zero completed items in the window returns an explicit empty result rather than zero or null ambiguity
The calculation reads a frozen done-event timestamp rather than deriving it live from current record state
Unit tests cover: normal population, zero completions in the window, and a record edited after its done event
technicalDependencies: A captured, immutable done-event timestamp per artifact type (Mark Complete, owner approval, suite ready)
nonFunctionalRequirements: A later edit to a completed artifact's record must not change a previously computed median

items.title: Compute developer-to-production cycle time
items.description: Build the calculation that joins each linked work item's first developer-start event (My Work session start, or Azure DevOps In Progress/Active) to its Release's production deployment timestamp, restricted to work items linked to a Release that has recorded a production deployment, and computes the rolling 90-day median across the project.
definitionOfDone: Median spans first developer-start to Release production deployment for linked items only
Items linked to a Release with only Development or Staging deployments are excluded
The 90-day window and project scope match the other cycle-time tiles
Unit tests cover: a normal linked-and-deployed set, an item linked to a non-production-only Release, and no qualifying deployments in the window
nonFunctionalRequirements: Work items not linked to a Release with a recorded production deployment are excluded from the median rather than counted as zero

items.title: Aggregate open bugs on PBIs from Azure DevOps
items.description: Build the aggregation that reads Azure DevOps child-Bug relationships for PBIs in the active project, excludes Bugs whose state is Done, Closed, Resolved, or Removed, and returns per-PBI open-bug counts plus a project total.
definitionOfDone: A Bug counts as open unless its state is Done, Closed, Resolved, or Removed
Only Bugs that are children of a PBI are counted; Feature- or Epic-level rollups are not produced
Returns a per-PBI count and a project total
Unit tests cover: a PBI with a mix of open and closed Bugs, a PBI with zero Bugs, and a Bug related but not a child of a PBI
technicalDependencies: Azure DevOps work-item parent/child relationship data
nonFunctionalRequirements: Only child-of-PBI Bugs are counted; Bugs related by other link types (related, duplicate) are excluded

items.title: Build dashboard tile components and client data hooks
items.description: Build the five dashboard tile components that render as the Agent Home main canvas, each independently gated by its underlying module's permission, sorting list rows oldest-last-updated first with a 20-row cap and a "View all" link, and reusing existing detail routes for drill-through (a Test Case row opens its parent PRD).
definitionOfDone: Each of the five tiles renders only when the caller holds its underlying module's permission
List tiles show empty-state copy when there are zero rows instead of hiding the tile
KPI tiles show an em dash and a "No completed items in the last 90 days" note when the 90-day set is empty
Rows and "View all" links navigate to the existing Interview/PRD/Calendar/Releases routes
Unit and integration tests cover: full data, empty data, and missing-permission for each tile
nonFunctionalRequirements: Each tile hides independently based on the caller's permission for its underlying module, with no dashboard-specific permission

items.title: View the incomplete pipeline queue

userStory.iWant: see every Interview, PRD, Test Case, Design Prototype, and Design Doc that is still in flight in the current project
userStory.soThat: I can spot stalled work without opening Backlog first

outOfScope: An All/Mine toggle on the Incomplete Pipeline tile
A dedicated Test Case detail route

acceptanceCriteria.then: the Incomplete Pipeline card lists each open group with its count and up to 20 rows sorted oldest-updated-first, plus a "View all" link per group
acceptanceCriteria.given: I have access to Interview today and there are incomplete Interviews, PRDs, Test Cases, Prototypes, or Design Docs in the current project

acceptanceCriteria.then: the Incomplete Pipeline card shows a retry-capable error state instead of a blank or crashed tile
acceptanceCriteria.given: the pipeline data fails to load

acceptanceCriteria.then: each pipeline group shows a short empty-state line instead of the card being hidden
acceptanceCriteria.given: the current project has no incomplete artifacts

acceptanceCriteria.then: the Incomplete Pipeline card does not render at all
acceptanceCriteria.given: I do not have interviews:view or cannot open the Interview menu today

nonFunctionalRequirements.security: Rows and counts are limited to the current project and to callers with interviews:view; no cross-project data is returned
nonFunctionalRequirements.performance: Incomplete Pipeline payload completes within 2 seconds at P95 under 100 concurrent Home loads
nonFunctionalRequirements.accessibility: Group headers, counts, and rows are screen-reader labeled and reachable by keyboard to their destination route

items.title: View artifact cycle time

userStory.iWant: see the median time each artifact type takes from creation to its own done event
userStory.soThat: I can judge how quickly design work moves through the pipeline without leaving Home

outOfScope: Row-level lists on the Artifact Cycle Time card — it stays KPI-only

acceptanceCriteria.then: the Artifact Cycle Time card shows each type's median days from creation to its own done event
acceptanceCriteria.given: completed Interviews, PRDs, Test Cases, Prototypes, and Design Docs exist in the last 90 days

acceptanceCriteria.then: that KPI shows an error indicator while the other KPIs on the card still render normally
acceptanceCriteria.given: the cycle-time computation fails for one artifact type

acceptanceCriteria.then: that KPI shows an em dash and a "No completed items in the last 90 days" note
acceptanceCriteria.given: no artifact of a given type reached its done event in the last 90 days

acceptanceCriteria.then: the Prototype cycle-time KPI does not appear on the card
acceptanceCriteria.given: Design Prototypes are disabled for the current project

nonFunctionalRequirements.security: Median values reflect only the current project's artifacts
nonFunctionalRequirements.performance: Artifact Cycle Time payload completes within 2 seconds at P95
nonFunctionalRequirements.accessibility: Each KPI value and its label are exposed to screen readers as a single readable unit

items.title: View My Work status and cycle time

userStory.iWant: see my own Ready and In Progress counts and how long my completed items take to finish
userStory.soThat: I can gauge my personal workload from Home without opening My Work

outOfScope: Team-wide My Work totals — the tile is self-only

acceptanceCriteria.then: the My Work tile shows my Ready and In Progress counts plus my median time to Mark Complete or Azure DevOps Done/Closed over the last 90 days
acceptanceCriteria.given: I am in the Developer group with items in Ready or In Progress

acceptanceCriteria.then: the tile shows a retry-capable error state
acceptanceCriteria.given: the My Work data fails to load

acceptanceCriteria.then: the cycle-time number shows an em dash and the 90-day note while the counts still display
acceptanceCriteria.given: I have no completed items in the last 90 days

acceptanceCriteria.then: the My Work tile does not render
acceptanceCriteria.given: I cannot open My Work today (missing dev-workbench:view or Developer group membership)

nonFunctionalRequirements.security: The endpoint returns only the signed-in user's own items; requests for another user's items are rejected
nonFunctionalRequirements.performance: My Work payload completes within 2 seconds at P95
nonFunctionalRequirements.accessibility: Counts and the cycle-time value are announced with their unit (days) to screen readers

items.title: View open bugs on PBIs

userStory.iWant: see which PBIs in the current project have open child Bugs and how many
userStory.soThat: I can gauge defect load without opening Calendar first

outOfScope: Bugs related to a PBI by link types other than child (related, duplicate)
Rolling bug counts up to Feature or Epic level

acceptanceCriteria.then: the Open Bugs on PBIs tile lists up to 20 PBIs sorted oldest-updated-first with their open-bug counts and a project total
acceptanceCriteria.given: at least one PBI in the current project has an open child Bug

acceptanceCriteria.then: the tile shows a retry-capable error state instead of a stale or blank count
acceptanceCriteria.given: the Azure DevOps query for open Bugs fails

acceptanceCriteria.then: the tile stays visible with empty-list copy rather than being hidden
acceptanceCriteria.given: no PBI in the project has an open child Bug

acceptanceCriteria.then: the Open Bugs on PBIs tile does not render
acceptanceCriteria.given: I do not have calendar:view

nonFunctionalRequirements.security: Bug counts are limited to the current project's PBIs; no Bug description text or reviewer identity is exposed
nonFunctionalRequirements.performance: Bug tile payload completes within 5 seconds at P95 against Azure DevOps, or shows the last-known counts when ADO is slow
nonFunctionalRequirements.accessibility: PBI rows and counts are keyboard-navigable to Calendar

items.title: View developer-to-production cycle time

userStory.iWant: see the project-wide median time from a developer's first start to a linked Release reaching production
userStory.soThat: I can track delivery speed from Home and jump into Releases when it looks off

outOfScope: A list of linked work items inside the tile — it stays KPI-only

acceptanceCriteria.then: the tile shows the project-wide median time from developer start to that Release's production deployment, and clicking the tile opens Releases
acceptanceCriteria.given: work items linked to a Release with a production deployment exist in the last 90 days

acceptanceCriteria.then: the tile shows a retry-capable error state
acceptanceCriteria.given: the Releases data fails to load

acceptanceCriteria.then: the tile shows an em dash and the 90-day note
acceptanceCriteria.given: no linked work item's Release recorded a production deployment in the last 90 days

acceptanceCriteria.then: the Developer-to-production tile does not render
acceptanceCriteria.given: I do not have planning:releases

nonFunctionalRequirements.security: The median is computed only from the current project's linked work items and Releases
nonFunctionalRequirements.performance: Developer-to-production payload completes within 5 seconds at P95 against Releases/Azure DevOps, or shows the last-known median when slow
nonFunctionalRequirements.accessibility: The KPI value and its 90-day scope are announced together to screen readers

features.title: Pipeline Status Dashboard
outOfScope: An All/Mine toggle on any pipeline tile
A new Test Case detail page or route
A new RBAC permission for the dashboard — every tile reuses its underlying module's existing permission
features.description: Gives BA, Manager, Developer, QA, and Project Admin a project-status view on Agent Home: BA and Manager see open pipeline artifacts and how long they take to finish, Developer sees their own Ready/In-Progress load, QA sees open Bugs sitting on PBIs, and Project Admin sees developer-to-production delivery time.

Existing My Work Ready/In-Progress session data
Azure DevOps child-Bug relationships and Release production deployment records

personaBehaviors.behavior: View open pipeline artifacts and cycle time to completion

View open bugs associated with PBIs

items.title: Move the Home chat composer, skill pills, and thread history into the slide-out
items.description: Extract the Agent Home compose experience — composer, skill pills, MCP pills, and thread history — from the page body into the existing chat-panel component, so Home's main canvas renders the dashboard and a right-edge toggle opens that panel, closed by default.
definitionOfDone: Home's main canvas renders the dashboard by default with chat closed
A right-edge toggle opens the panel containing the composer, skill pills, MCP pills, and thread history
The toggle is hidden for a caller without chat:view
Unit tests cover: toggle open/close, panel content parity with the prior full-page layout, and the hidden-without-permission case
technicalDependencies: The existing chat-panel component and its underlying chat session hook
nonFunctionalRequirements: The toggle and panel require chat:view/chat:create; no new permission is introduced

items.title: Restyle and share the slide-out shell across Home, PRD Assistant, Design Doc Assistant, and Calendar Work-Item Assistant
items.description: Apply one shared frame — header with title/close, transcript, and bottom composer — uniformly to Agent Home Chat, PRD Assistant, Design Doc Assistant, and Calendar Work-Item Assistant, while each assistant keeps its own additional actions (PRD diff review, calendar confirm-before-write). Add a full-height overlay presentation for narrow viewports, replacing the fixed-width side panel there.
definitionOfDone: All four panels share the same frame, transcript, and bottom composer styling
Each assistant's extra actions still render and function inside the shared frame
On narrow viewports all four panels present as a full-height overlay instead of a fixed-width side panel
Visual regression or component tests cover all four panels on both desktop and narrow viewports
technicalDependencies: Each assistant's existing extra-action UI (diff review, confirm-before-write)
nonFunctionalRequirements: Each assistant's existing confirm-before-write and diff-review gates continue to run unchanged inside the shared shell

items.title: Keep the active thread alive when the slide-out is closed
items.description: Change the panel's Close action to hide the panel without ending the active conversation thread, so reopening the panel resumes the same thread. New Chat continues to start a fresh thread as it does today.
definitionOfDone: Close hides the panel and leaves the underlying thread open
Reopening the panel after Close resumes the same thread with its prior messages
New Chat still starts a new thread regardless of Close's changed behavior
Unit tests cover: close-then-reopen resuming the same thread, and New Chat starting a distinct thread
nonFunctionalRequirements: Closing the panel must not issue a thread-ending call to the server

items.title: Open and resume Agent Home Chat from a slide-out toggle

userStory.iWant: open Agent Home Chat from a right-edge toggle and pick up where I left off
userStory.soThat: I can check delivery status first and only open a conversation when I actually need one

outOfScope: A second floating action button
A header chat entry point on Home — Home keeps only the right-edge toggle

acceptanceCriteria.then: the shared slide-out opens over the dashboard with the composer, skill pills, MCP pills, and thread history, and closing it returns me to the dashboard
acceptanceCriteria.when: I click the right-edge Chat toggle
acceptanceCriteria.given: I have chat:view on Agent Home

acceptanceCriteria.then: it shows a reconnecting or error status instead of an unresponsive panel
acceptanceCriteria.given: the chat session fails to connect

acceptanceCriteria.then: the same thread resumes instead of starting over
acceptanceCriteria.given: I close the slide-out mid-conversation

acceptanceCriteria.then: the right-edge Chat toggle does not render
acceptanceCriteria.given: I do not have chat:view

nonFunctionalRequirements.security: Panel access still requires chat:view/chat:create; no new permission is introduced
nonFunctionalRequirements.performance: The slide-out opens or closes within 300ms of the toggle click, independent of chat response time
nonFunctionalRequirements.accessibility: The toggle and panel are keyboard-operable and the panel is announced as a complementary region on open

items.title: Experience a consistent slide-out shell across Home and existing assistants

userStory.iWant: see the same panel frame, transcript, and composer whether I open Agent Home Chat, PRD Assistant, Design Doc Assistant, or Calendar Work-Item Assistant
userStory.soThat: switching between AI side panels in Apex feels familiar instead of like four different tools

outOfScope: New Cursor-only chrome such as a mode picker, @-file mentions, or checkpoints
Making Interview, ADR, or Standup chat into slide-outs

acceptanceCriteria.then: all four use the same frame, transcript, and bottom composer, and each keeps its own extra actions (PRD diff review, calendar confirm-before-write)
acceptanceCriteria.given: I open Agent Home Chat, PRD Assistant, Design Doc Assistant, or Calendar Work-Item Assistant on a desktop viewport

acceptanceCriteria.then: the shared shell still renders the transcript and composer with an inline error for the failed section
acceptanceCriteria.given: the panel fails to load its extra actions (for example diff data)

acceptanceCriteria.then: it presents as a full-height overlay over the underlying page, and closing it returns to that page
acceptanceCriteria.given: I open any of the four panels on a narrow viewport

acceptanceCriteria.then: it does not show Home-only elements (skill pills, MCP pills, or thread history)
acceptanceCriteria.given: I open the Calendar Work-Item Assistant

nonFunctionalRequirements.security: Each assistant keeps its existing confirm-before-write and diff-review gates; the shared shell introduces no new data exposure
nonFunctionalRequirements.performance: The shared shell renders within 300ms of the assistant's existing open action, matching current panel responsiveness
nonFunctionalRequirements.accessibility: Panel title, close control, and composer are reachable by keyboard and labeled for screen readers across all four assistants

epics.description: Agent Home opens on a chat box today and gives no view of project delivery status. This epic replaces the Home landing canvas with a five-tile status dashboard (open pipeline artifacts, artifact cycle time, personal work, PBI bugs, and developer-to-production time) and relocates chat into an on-demand slide-out shared by the existing document and work-item assistants.
successMetrics: A user can see project delivery status on Agent Home without sending a chat message
Pipeline stalls (a Mark Complete Interview with no PRD yet, an approved Prototype with no Design Doc yet) are visible on Home without navigating to Backlog
Agent Home Chat, PRD Assistant, Design Doc Assistant, and Calendar Work-Item Assistant present the same slide-out frame, transcript, and composer

businessRules.rule: The Incomplete Pipeline tile includes an Interview only while it is in_progress, or Mark Complete with no PRD generated yet for it; archived Interviews are excluded.
A PRD, Design Prototype, or Design Doc counts as incomplete until owner final approval; reviewer-only approval (Awaiting Owner Approval) keeps it on the tile.

A PRD's Test Case row is incomplete only when the PRD requires a QA suite and that suite is missing, generating, or failed; a PRD with testCasesRequired false is omitted from the Test Case group entirely.
An owner-approved Design Prototype stays in the Prototype group of the Incomplete Pipeline tile until a Design Doc row exists for that feature, even if generation has not started.
When Design Prototypes are disabled for the current project, the Prototype group is hidden from the Incomplete Pipeline tile and the Prototype median is hidden from the Artifact Cycle Time tile.
Incomplete Pipeline rows and Open Bugs on PBIs rows sort oldest-last-updated first, cap at 20 rows per group or list, and show a project total plus a "View all" link.

Artifact cycle time is the median time from creation to that artifact's own done event (Interview Mark Complete; PRD, Design Prototype, and Design Doc owner final approval; Test Case suite ready) over completed items in the last 90 days; it never includes downstream stall time from the Incomplete Pipeline tile's stall-aware rule.
My Work Ready and In Progress counts, and the median cycle time to Mark Complete or Azure DevOps Done/Closed, are scoped to the signed-in user only, in the current project, over the last 90 days.
businessRules.appliesTo: View My Work status and cycle time

businessRules.rule: A Bug counts as open on the Open Bugs on PBIs tile unless its Azure DevOps state is Done, Closed, Resolved, or Removed; the tile lists only PBIs with at least one open child Bug.

Developer-to-production cycle time is the median time from first developer start (My Work session start, or Azure DevOps In Progress/Active) to a linked Release's production deployment timestamp, over the last 90 days, project-wide; work items not linked to a Release with a production deployment are excluded.

A pipeline row navigates to its existing detail route (Interview, PRD, Design Prototype, or Design Doc); a Test Case row opens its parent PRD; each group's "View all" opens the matching Interviews & PRDs tab.
The Incomplete Pipeline and Artifact Cycle Time tiles are hidden unless the signed-in user can open Interview today (interviews:view plus Interview menu visibility, Super Admin excepted).
The My Work tile is hidden unless the signed-in user is in the Developer group and holds dev-workbench:view.
businessRules.appliesTo: View My Work status and cycle time

businessRules.rule: The Open Bugs on PBIs tile is hidden without calendar:view; the Developer-to-production tile is hidden without planning:releases. Neither tile is hidden based on the project's name.
Closing the Agent Home or header Agent Chat panel hides the panel and preserves the active thread so reopening it resumes the same conversation; New Chat still starts a fresh thread.
businessRules.appliesTo: Open and resume Agent Home Chat from a slide-out toggle

businessRules.rule: The shared slide-out is a right-side overlay on desktop viewports and a full-height overlay on narrow viewports for Agent Home Chat, PRD Assistant, Design Doc Assistant, and Calendar Work-Item Assistant; each assistant keeps its own additional actions on top of the shared frame.
businessRules.appliesTo: Experience a consistent slide-out shell across Home and existing assistants

implementationPhases.rationale: This PRD scopes a single epic, so all work executes in one phase. Within it, Feature 1 (Pipeline Status Dashboard) builds the aggregation services and tiles that become the new Home main canvas, and Feature 2 (Shared Cursor-like Slide-out Chat) depends on that canvas existing before its right-edge toggle and shared shell can be placed on it — expressed as FEAT-002.dependsOn = [FEAT-001] rather than as a separate phase, since both features belong to the same epic and are delivered together.
